subject: Post-demo: narrow trial proposal & acceptance gates
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Walsh <jordan.walsh@aureliadata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: narrow trial proposal & acceptance gates

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo and for walking us through the three representative workflows (inbound triage, customer Q/A, and claim extraction). Quick recap + a concrete narrow-scope trial we recommend to validate parity vs your current in-house baseline.

What we propose (4-week narrow pilot):
- Scope: 300–500 representative customer queries across the three workflows (we can take a 100-sample seed you provide and augment).
- Models to trial (initial):
  - Open candidates: Mistral-Instruct-7B (instruct-tuned, 8-bit quant) and Llama-3-13B (8-bit/quantized variant).
  - Baseline: your current production model (you mentioned "AureliaCore-v3") for head-to-head.
- Acceptance gates (high level):
  - Intent/slot accuracy: >=94% intent accuracy and >=0.92 F1 on key extraction fields.
  - Hallucination / critical error rate: <=2% on a manually labeled critical set.
  - Latency: median generation time <= 450ms end-to-end for single-request path (streaming allowed).
- Data & instrumentation we need: 300 sample queries, ground-truth labels for the critical set (if available), and a short list of high-risk utterances you want to protect against.

Attachments: I attached a starter prompt bundle and a short latency/memory estimate for the two model families.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you share the 300-sample CSV and confirm whether we can run the trial in our sandbox or if you prefer us to test against a snapshot you host?
2) Any constraints on data residency / redaction we should follow?
3) If this plan looks reasonable, we propose starting the week of July 5 — we’ll send a kickoff calendar invite and a short test plan.

Marissa and Priyom — looping you both to own prompt tuning and evaluation harness. Vivek — adding you for resource & pricing guidance.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to tighten scope.

—
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- Aurelia_trial_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 12KB)
- trial-scope-latency-memory-estimates.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: narrow trial proposal & acceptance gates

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications before we commit the sample set: 
- We use "AureliaCore-v3" internally for routing + post-processing; we can provide a sandbox snapshot. Would Redwood need direct access to our sandbox, or can we push the sample set and you run everything on your infra?
- On the acceptance gates: the 94% intent target looks reasonable, but our product team will push for a higher extraction F1 on the financial entities (we depend on those). Can you show how you’ll measure F1 (tooling + human review bandwidth)?
- Budget: can you provide a rough order-of-magnitude for compute / trial cost for trying both open candidates? That will help me get quick approval from procurement.

We’ve signed the NDA already (completed last week). If positive, we’re hopeful this moves to a pilot budget in Q3.

Jordan Walsh
Head of Product — Aurelia Data
jordan.walsh@aureliadata.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: narrow trial proposal & acceptance gates (prompt sets + bench links)

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick questions. I’m Marissa (solutions / eval ops) — I’ll run the evaluation harness and own the comparison to your baseline. Quick runbook and resources below so we’re aligned on measurement and human-review needs.

1) Where we run the test
- Option A (faster): You push the 300-sample CSV (anonymized) to the Drive link below and we run everything on Redwood sandbox infra. We will not store PII and will respect your redaction flags.
- Option B (if you prefer): We provide a Docker test harness you run against your snapshot and send results back.

2) Measurement & tooling
- Intent accuracy: measured via automatic matching against your supplied intent labels; we’ll surface a per-intent confusion matrix.
- Field extraction: exact-match + token-level F1. We’ll also run a manual spot-check (5–10% of samples) for critical fields — that’s where human review time matters. Plan: 30–50 two-hour reviews across the set (~6–8 hours of reviewer time).
- Hallucination / critical-error audit: we’ll create a 50-example "critical set" from your historical failures; those will be manually labeled and used as a gate.

3) Candidate models & tuning notes
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (huggingface link below): good strong baseline for instruction-style Q/A; tends to be cost-effective and fast to run. Quantization (8-bit) gives large cost savings but track for small edge-case drop in numeric fidelity.
- Llama-3-13B (HF link below): usually closer to your proprietary baseline on conversational coherence but higher memory footprint. We will test 13B 8-bit and a 13B 4-bit quantized variant if latency/VRAM allows.
- Redwood-configured fallback: if a candidate fails the critical set, we’ll test a routing policy that falls back to a higher-capacity variant only for those queries (keeps cost low while preserving safety).

4) Acceptance testing and regression control
- Primary gates (must pass): Intent >=94%, Field extraction F1 >=0.92, Critical-set error rate <=2%.
- Secondary checks (informational): ROUGE-L and a human preference ballot (N=100) comparing responses side-by-side.
- Regression control: we’ll run a canned prompt-set across both model candidates and your baseline; any drop >3% relative for an important metric triggers a manual review and roll-back.

5) Links & artifacts (starter pack)
- Prompt bundle (starter): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-aurelia-trials
- Mistral candidate: https://huggingface.co/mistralai/mistral-instruct-7b
- Llama-3 candidate: https://huggingface.co/facebook/llama-3-13b
- Redwood bench dashboard (read-only): https://redwood.internal/bench/dashboard?rid=RDW-2027-AUR-09
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

6) Cost / compute estimates (Vivek to add details)

Priyom — I attached the initial prompt CSV and a short PDF with latency+memory back-of-envelope. Vivek — can you confirm a rough delta in monthly cost for trying both candidates for 4 weeks? Jordan — if you prefer, we can provide a scoped PO estimate after we confirm run mode.

If that all looks good we’ll send a kickoff agenda + calendar invite for July 6.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions & Eval Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
